questions.q:
Let $A = [a_{ij}]$ be a square matrix of order $3 \times 3$, where the elements are defined as
$a_{ij} = \begin{cases} i - 2j & \text{if } i = j \\ 0 & \text{if } i \gt j \\ 1 & \text{if } i \lt j \end{cases}$ then the value of $|A^t|$ is
questions.solution:
Given the elements of the $3 \times 3$ matrix $A = [a_{ij}]$:

For the diagonal elements ($i = j$):
$a_{11} = 1 - 2(1) = -1$
$a_{22} = 2 - 2(2) = -2$
$a_{33} = 3 - 2(3) = -3$

For elements below the principal diagonal ($i \gt j$):
$a_{21} = 0, a_{31} = 0, a_{32} = 0$

For elements above the principal diagonal ($i \lt j$):
$a_{12} = 1, a_{13} = 1, a_{23} = 1$

Constructing the matrix $A$, we get:
$A = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 \end{bmatrix}$

Since $A$ is an upper triangular matrix, its determinant is simply the product of its principal diagonal elements:
$|A| = (-1) \times (-2) \times (-3) = -6$

Using the property of determinants that the determinant of a matrix is equal to the determinant of its transpose, we have:
$|A^t| = |A| = -6$

Answer: $-6$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let A be a square matrix of order $3 \times 3$. If $|A| = -4$, then the value of $\left|\dfrac{A^{-1}}{-2}\right|$ is:
questions.solution:
Given $A$ is a $3 \times 3$ matrix and $|A| = -4$.

Using the property of determinants $|kA| = k^n |A|$ where $n$ is the order of the matrix, we get:

$\left|\dfrac{A^{-1}}{-2}\right| = \left|-\dfrac{1}{2} A^{-1}\right| = \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^3 |A^{-1}|$

Since $|A^{-1}| = \dfrac{1}{|A|}$:

Substituting $|A| = -4$, we get $|A^{-1}| = -\dfrac{1}{4}$.

Therefore, $\left|\dfrac{A^{-1}}{-2}\right| = \left(-\dfrac{1}{8}\right) \times \left(-\dfrac{1}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{32}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{32}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Given $P = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & \alpha & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$ is the adjoint of a $3 \times 3$ matrix A and $|A| = 3$, then the value of $\alpha$ is:
questions.solution:
Given $P = \text{adj}(A)$ and $A$ is a $3 \times 3$ matrix.

We know that $|\text{adj}(A)| = |A|^{n-1}$, where $n$ is the order of the matrix.

Here, $n = 3$ and $|A| = 3$.

$|P| = |A|^{3-1} = |A|^2 = 3^2 = 9$

Now, calculating the determinant of matrix $P$:

$|P| = \begin{vmatrix} 2 & \alpha & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & 3 \end{vmatrix}$

Expanding along the first row:

$|P| = 2(2 \times 3 - 2 \times 3) - \alpha(1 \times 3 - 2 \times 1) + 1(1 \times 3 - 2 \times 1)$

$|P| = 2(0) - \alpha(1) + 1(1)$

$|P| = 1 - \alpha$

Equating the two values of $|P|$:

$1 - \alpha = 9$

$\alpha = -8$

Answer: $-8$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The cofactor of the element $a_{21}$ in the expansion of $\Delta=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & 4 & 4 \\ -3 & 5 & 9 \\ 2 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right|$ is
questions.solution:
The element $a_{21}$ is the element in the second row and first column of the determinant $\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 4 & 4 \\ -3 & 5 & 9 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \end{vmatrix}$.

The value of $a_{21}$ is $-3$.

The cofactor $C_{ij}$ of an element $a_{ij}$ is given by $(-1)^{i+j} M_{ij}$, where $M_{ij}$ is the minor obtained by deleting the $i$-th row and $j$-th column.

For $a_{21}$, we have $i=2$ and $j=1$. Thus, the cofactor is $C_{21} = (-1)^{2+1} M_{21} = -M_{21}$.

The minor $M_{21}$ is the determinant of the matrix formed by removing the second row and first column:

$M_{21} = \begin{vmatrix} 4 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 \end{vmatrix} = (4 \times 2) - (4 \times 1) = 8 - 4 = 4$.

Therefore, the cofactor $C_{21} = -M_{21} = -4$.

Answer: $-4$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
The cost of 4 kg onion, 3 kg wheat and 2 kg rice is ₹ 500.
The cost of 1 kg onion, 2 kg wheat and 3 kg rice is ₹ 300 .
The cost of 6 kg onion, 2 kg wheat and 3 kg rice is ₹ 575 .
The above situation can be represented in matrix form as $\mathrm{AX}=\mathrm{B}$. Then $\left|5 A^{-1}\right|=$
questions.solution:
Let $x, y, z$ be the cost per kg of onion, wheat, and rice respectively. The given system of linear equations is:

$4x + 3y + 2z = 500$
$x + 2y + 3z = 300$
$6x + 2y + 3z = 575$

The matrix $A$ is given by:
$A = \begin{pmatrix} 4 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 6 & 2 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$

Calculate the determinant $|A|$:
$|A| = 4(2 \times 3 - 3 \times 2) - 3(1 \times 3 - 3 \times 6) + 2(1 \times 2 - 2 \times 6)$
$|A| = 4(6 - 6) - 3(3 - 18) + 2(2 - 12)$
$|A| = 4(0) - 3(-15) + 2(-10)$
$|A| = 0 + 45 - 20 = 25$

We need to find $|5A^{-1}|$. Using the property $|kA| = k^n |A|$ where $n$ is the order of the matrix:
$|5A^{-1}| = 5^3 |A^{-1}| = 125 \times \dfrac{1}{|A|}$

$|5A^{-1}| = 125 \times \dfrac{1}{25} = 5$

Answer: 5

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Value of the determinant of a matrix A of order $3 \times 3$ is 7 . Then the value of the determinant formed by the cofactors of matrix A is
questions.solution:
Let $A$ be a square matrix of order $n \times n$. The matrix formed by the cofactors of $A$ is denoted by $C$. The property relating the determinant of the cofactor matrix to the determinant of the original matrix is given by $|C| = |A|^{n-1}$.

In this problem, the order of matrix $A$ is $n = 3$ and the determinant of $A$ is $|A| = 7$.

Substituting these values into the formula:

$|C| = 7^{3-1} = 7^2 = 49$.

Answer: $49$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
The sum of three numbers is 6 .
Twice the third number, when added to the first number gives 7 ,
On adding the sum of the second and third numbers to thrice the first number, we get 12 .
The above situation can be represented in matrix form as $A X=B$.
Then the $|\operatorname{adj} A|$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let the three numbers be $x, y, z$.

The given conditions are:
1. $x + y + z = 6$
2. $x + 0y + 2z = 7$
3. $3x + y + z = 12$

The system of equations in matrix form $AX = B$ is:
$\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 6 \\ 7 \\ 12 \end{pmatrix}$

Calculate the determinant of matrix $A$:
$|A| = 1(0 - 2) - 1(1 - 6) + 1(1 - 0)$
$|A| = -2 + 5 + 1 = 4$

The property of the adjoint matrix is $|\operatorname{adj} A| = |A|^{n-1}$, where $n$ is the order of the matrix.
Here $n = 3$, so $|\operatorname{adj} A| = |A|^{3-1} = |A|^2$.

$|\operatorname{adj} A| = 4^2 = 16$.

Answer: $16$

$\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
\cos (\alpha+\beta) & -\sin (\alpha+\beta) & \cos 2 \beta \\
\sin \alpha & \cos \alpha & \sin \beta \\
-\cos \alpha & \sin \alpha & \cos \beta
\end{array}\right|
$ is independent of
questions.solution:
Apply $C_1 \to C_1\cos\beta + C_2\sin\beta$ and $C_2 \to -C_1\sin\beta + C_2\cos\beta$:

$\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} \cos(\alpha+2\beta) & -\sin(\alpha+2\beta) & \cos2\beta \\ \sin(\alpha+\beta) & \cos(\alpha+\beta) & \sin\beta \\ -\cos(\alpha+\beta) & \sin(\alpha+\beta) & \cos\beta \end{vmatrix}$

Expanding along first row:

$\Delta = \cos(\alpha+2\beta)[\cos(\alpha+\beta)\cos\beta - \sin(\alpha+\beta)\sin\beta]$
$+ \sin(\alpha+2\beta)[\sin(\alpha+\beta)\cos\beta + \cos(\alpha+\beta)\sin\beta]$
$+ \cos2\beta[\sin^2(\alpha+\beta) + \cos^2(\alpha+\beta)]$

$= \cos(\alpha+2\beta)\cos(\alpha+2\beta) + \sin(\alpha+2\beta)\sin(\alpha+2\beta) + \cos2\beta$

$= \cos^2(\alpha+2\beta) + \sin^2(\alpha+2\beta) + \cos2\beta$

$= 1 + \cos2\beta$

Result depends on $\beta$ but is independent of $\alpha$.

questions.q: If $A=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}0 & x & 16 \\ x & 5 & 7 \\ 0 & 9 & x\end{array}\right]$ is a singular matrix then $x$ is equal to
questions.solution:
For singular matrix, $|A| = 0$

Expanding along first column (two zeros):

$|A| = 0 - x\begin{vmatrix} x & 16 \\ 9 & x \end{vmatrix} + 0$

$= -x(x^2 - 144)$

Setting $|A| = 0$:

$-x(x^2 - 144) = 0$

$x = 0$ or $x = \pm 12$

Among the given options, $x = -12$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\left[\begin{array}{ccc}2+x & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 \\ x & 1 & -5\end{array}\right]$ is a singular matrix, then $x$ is
questions.solution:
A matrix is singular if its determinant is equal to zero. Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2+x & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 \\ x & 1 & -5 \end{bmatrix}$.

The determinant $|A|$ is given by:

$|A| = (2+x) \begin{vmatrix} -1 & 2 \\ 1 & -5 \end{vmatrix} - 3 \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ x & -5 \end{vmatrix} + 4 \begin{vmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ x & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 0$

Calculating the $2 \times 2$ determinants:

$|A| = (2+x)(5 - 2) - 3(-5 - 2x) + 4(1 - (-x)) = 0$

$|A| = (2+x)(3) - 3(-5 - 2x) + 4(1 + x) = 0$

Expanding the terms:

$6 + 3x + 15 + 6x + 4 + 4x = 0$

Combining like terms:

$13x + 25 = 0$

$13x = -25$

$x = -\dfrac{25}{13}$

Answer: $-\dfrac{25}{13}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $A=\left[\begin{array}{cc}k+1 & 2 \\ 4 & k-1\end{array}\right]$ is a singular matrix, then possible values of $\mathrm{k}$ are
questions.solution:
A matrix $A$ is singular if its determinant is zero, i.e., $|A| = 0$.

Given $A = \begin{bmatrix} k+1 & 2 \\ 4 & k-1 \end{bmatrix}$, the determinant is calculated as:

$|A| = (k+1)(k-1) - (2)(4)$

$|A| = (k^2 - 1) - 8$

$|A| = k^2 - 9$

Setting the determinant to zero for a singular matrix:

$k^2 - 9 = 0$

$k^2 = 9$

$k = \pm 3$

Answer: $\pm 3$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $A=\left[\begin{array}{cc}2-k & 2 \\ 1 & 3-k\end{array}\right]$ is a singular matrix, then the value of $5 k-k^2$ is
questions.solution:
A matrix $A$ is singular if its determinant is zero, so $\det(A) = 0$.

Given $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2-k & 2 \\ 1 & 3-k \end{bmatrix}$, the determinant is calculated as:

$\det(A) = (2-k)(3-k) - (2)(1) = 0$

Expanding the expression:

$6 - 2k - 3k + k^2 - 2 = 0$

$k^2 - 5k + 4 = 0$

Rearranging the terms to find the value of $5k - k^2$:

$k^2 - 5k = -4$

Multiplying by $-1$ gives:

$5k - k^2 = 4$

Answer: 4

The number of distinct real roots of
$\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\sin x & \cos x & \cos x \\ \cos x & \sin x & \cos x \\ \cos x & \cos x & \sin x\end{array}\right|$ in the interval $\left[\frac{-\pi}{4}, \frac{\pi}{4}\right]$ is
questions.solution:
$\left|\begin{array}{lll}\sin x & \cos x & \cos x \\ \cos x & \sin x & \cos x \\ \cos x & \cos x & \sin x\end{array}\right|=0$
Applying $C_{1} \rightarrow C_{1}+C_{2}+C_{3}\left|\begin{array}{lll}2 \cos x+\sin x & \cos x & \cos x \\ 2 \cos x+\sin x & \sin x & \cos x \\ 2 \cos x+\sin x & \cos x & \sin x\end{array}\right|=0\Rightarrow(2 \cos x+\sin x)\left|\begin{array}{lll}1 & \cos x & \cos x \\ 1 & \sin x & \cos x \\ 1 & \cos x & \sin x\end{array}\right|=0$
[Applying $R_{2} \rightarrow R_{2}-R_{1}$ and $R_{3} \rightarrow R_{3}-R_{1}$, we get $(2 \cos x+\sin x)\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & \cos x & \cos x \\ 0 & \sin x-\cos x & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \sin x-\cos x\end{array}\right|=0\Rightarrow(2 \cos x+\sin x)\left[1 \cdot(\sin -\cos x)^{2}\right]=0\Rightarrow(2 \cos x+\sin x)(\sin x-\cos x)^{2}=0\Rightarrow 2 \cos x=-\sin x$ or $\sin x=\cos x\Rightarrow \tan x=-2$ which is not possible as for
$-\frac{\pi}{4} \leq x \leq \frac{\pi}{4}$, we get $-1 \leq \tan x \leq 1$
or $\quad \tan x=1$
So, $x=\frac{\pi}{4}$. Hence, only one real root exist.

Let $\Delta=\left|\begin{array}{lll}x+2 & x+3 & x+2 a \\ x+3 & x+4 & x+2 b \\ x+4 & x+5 & x+2 c\end{array}\right|$
Applying $R_{2} \rightarrow 2 R_{2}$, we get

x+2 & x+3 & x+2 a \\
2 x+6 & 2 x+8 & 2 x+4 b \\

\Delta=\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
x+2 & x+3 & x+2 a \\
0 & 0 & 4 b-(2 a+2 c) \\
x+4 & x+5 & x+2 c
\end{array}\right|

$\Rightarrow \Delta=\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{array}{ccc}x+2 & x+3 & x+2 a \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ x+4 & x+5 & x+2 c\end{array}\right|\left[\begin{array}{c}\because a, b, c \text { are in AP } \\ \therefore 2 b=a+c\end{array}\right]\Rightarrow \Delta=0$

On applying, $C_{1} \rightarrow C_{1}-C_{2}, C_{2} \rightarrow C_{2}-C_{3}$, we get $\left|\begin{array}{rrr}-1 & -1 & 443 \\ -1 & -1 & 447 \\ -1 & -1 & 451\end{array}\right|=0\left[\because C_{1}\right.$ and $C_{2}$ are identical $]$

questions.q: If $A=\left[\begin{array}{cc}1 & \log _{b} a \\ \log _{a} b & 1\end{array}\right]$, then $|A|$ is equal to
questions.solution:
We have, $A=\left[\begin{array}{cc}1 & \log _{b} a \\ \log _{a} b & 1\end{array}\right]$
Now,

\begin{aligned}
|A| &=\left|\begin{array}{cc}
1 & \log _{b} a \\
\log _{a} b & 1
\end{array}\right| \\
&=1-\log _{a} b \log _{b} a \\
&=1-\log _{a} b \times \frac{1}{\log _{a} b}\left\{\because \log _{b} a=\frac{1}{\log _{a} b}\right\} \\
&=1-1=0
\end{aligned}
